report:
Finding: The difference points to a domain shift toward online news/blog/webpage content in Model B.

Reasoning:
- Across many high-norm late-layer cells (L18–L25), the logit-lens points strongly and repeatedly to tokens like “blogs”, “blogger”, “Blog”, “blogging”, “facebook”, “http”, “photo”, “video”, “film”, “News”, “TV”, “ads/ad”, “Mail”, “May/Mar”, parentheses and dashes, whitespace/newline tokens — all characteristic of web-page boilerplate, navigation, and media embeds.
- Topic nouns typical of news reporting are prominent at earlier/high-norm positions (e.g., “billionaire”, “politicians”, “journalists”, “spokesman/spokeswoman”, “chairman”, “legislators”, “Obama”), and generic metro/newspaper-style words (“metropolitan”) recur across layers.
- The signal concentrates in later layers and early token positions (p1–p4), consistent with a high-level bias that shapes surface token choices rather than low-level tokenization artifacts.

Conclusion: Model B appears more biased toward producing or recognizing news/blog/webpage-style text and site “chrome” (ads, media, dates, HTTP), relative to Model A. I cannot identify a specific training objective from this alone, but the domain difference (online news/blog/media) is strongly supported.
